headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks; no direct data-leak or compliance pathway is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a course repo with no runtime surfaces, while agent B processes PDF files and can run browsers. There is no documented shared channel, so direct injection is not proven; however, if A’s content is copied into PDFs or browser-rendered material that B ingests as instructions, the pathway exists in default document-processing workflows.
conditions: IF agent A content is placed into a PDF or browser-rendered document that agent B ingests as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF the operator manually bridges A’s outputs into B without sanitization, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Sanitize any A-derived text before B processes it.
Disable instruction-following on untrusted document text in B.
Use a strict content-to-data parser for PDFs.
Add provenance labels to all A-originated artifacts.
requires-engineering: isolate B’s browser tests from untrusted instructional content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A has no data classes touched and no filesystem or network egress beyond none; agent B touches PDF documents but also has no network egress. With no shared workspace or authenticated principal documented, there is no plausible leakage path from A to B in the provided profiles.
conditions: IF a shared workspace is later introduced between A and B, leakage analysis must be revisited.
IF either agent is given sensitive PDFs or files outside the current profiles, the risk profile changes.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Do not mount shared secrets into either agent.
Review any future file-sharing bridge before enabling it.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network surfaces documented, while B supports multiple instances and browser-based tests but no write permissions are listed. Overlap is therefore limited and no shared mutable resource is evidenced; uncertainty stays low because the profiles do not show conflicting write authority.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
IF either agent is connected to a shared mutable resource, coordination controls are needed.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Run B instances in separate sandboxes.
Add file-locking if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can consume PDF content and browser-test outputs, so if A-derived material is fed into B, B may render or act on it without verification. A itself is a course repo and does not execute actions, but the pair still supports a default pipeline where unverified A content can cascade into B’s outputs.
conditions: IF A-derived text is used as source material for B outputs without verification, cascading error risk is present.
IF B is configured to treat imported content as authoritative, the risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review of A-derived inputs before B uses them.
Add a verification step between A and B.
Mark imported content as untrusted in B.
Log source provenance for every B output.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for A, and B only lists PDF documents with no sensitive-data designation. Without a documented regulated-data flow, there is no compliance mismatch to assess between the pair.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into either agent, compliance must be reassessed.
IF residency or retention requirements are later specified, this verdict may change.
mitigations: Add retention and deletion policies if regulated data is introduced.
Review jurisdictional requirements before sharing files.
